node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limit notation
node.description: Interpret notation for the limit of a function as the input approaches a value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Graphical limits
node.description: Estimate and interpret limits from graphs, including behaviour near holes and jumps.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Numerical limits
node.description: Use tables of nearby input values to estimate limiting behaviour.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: One-sided limits
node.description: Distinguish left-hand and right-hand limits and use them to decide whether a two-sided limit exists.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limits by substitution
node.description: Evaluate limits by direct substitution when the function is continuous at the input value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Algebraic limit simplification
node.description: Simplify expressions to evaluate limits where direct substitution initially gives an indeterminate form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Continuity at a point
node.description: Determine whether a function is continuous at a point using function value, limit and agreement between them.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Discontinuity types introduction
node.description: Recognise removable, jump and infinite discontinuities from graphs and simple formulas.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Average rate of change
node.description: Calculate and interpret average rate of change over an interval as a secant gradient.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Instantaneous rate of change
node.description: Interpret instantaneous rate of change as a limiting value of average rates of change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative as tangent gradient
node.description: Interpret the derivative at a point as the gradient of the tangent to the graph at that point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative notation
node.description: Interpret common derivative notation such as f prime, dy/dx and derivative function notation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Power rule
node.description: Differentiate powers of x using the power rule and constant multiple rule.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sum and difference derivative rules
node.description: Differentiate sums and differences of differentiable functions term by term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Product and quotient rules
node.description: Use product and quotient rules to differentiate products and ratios of functions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Chain rule introduction
node.description: Differentiate composite functions using the chain rule in straightforward cases.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivatives of exponential and logarithmic functions
node.description: Differentiate common exponential and logarithmic functions and interpret their rates of change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
node.description: Differentiate sine, cosine and tangent functions in standard calculus contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limit describes nearby behaviour
node.description: A limit describes what function values approach as inputs get close to a value, not necessarily the function value at that point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Two-sided limit needs both sides
node.description: A two-sided limit exists only when left-hand and right-hand limits agree.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Continuity links value and limit
node.description: Continuity at a point requires the function value to exist and match the limiting value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative is limit of rates
node.description: A derivative is the limiting value of average rates of change over shrinking intervals.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative is tangent gradient
node.description: The derivative at a point gives the gradient of the tangent line at that point when it exists.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative function maps inputs to rates
node.description: A derivative function gives the instantaneous rate of change for each input where the derivative exists.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Chain rule handles composites
node.description: The chain rule differentiates a composite by combining the outer derivative with the inner derivative.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Limit equals function value
node.description: Learner assumes the limit at a point must equal the function value or cannot exist if the function value is missing.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: One-sided limit ignored
node.description: Learner claims a two-sided limit exists after checking only one side of the point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Derivative is y-value
node.description: Learner treats the derivative at a point as the function value rather than a rate or gradient.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Chain rule forgets inner derivative
node.description: Learner differentiates the outer function of a composite but omits multiplying by the inner derivative.

edge.rationale: Limit notation is foundational to limits and continuity.
Graphical limit interpretation directly practises limits and continuity.
Numerical limits support estimation of limiting behaviour.
One-sided limits determine when two-sided limits exist.
Substitution handles limits at continuity points.
Algebraic simplification is a common limit-evaluation strategy.
Continuity at a point applies function value and limit reasoning.
Discontinuity types are interpreted using limits and continuity conditions.
Average rate of change is the secant-rate basis for derivatives.
Instantaneous rate of change is central to derivative meaning.
Tangent gradient is a core graphical interpretation of derivatives.
Derivative notation is needed to communicate differentiation results.
The power rule is a foundational symbolic differentiation rule.
Sum and difference rules allow termwise differentiation.
Product and quotient rules handle combinations of functions.
The chain rule is central for differentiating composite functions.
Exponential and logarithmic derivatives are core senior differentiation cases.
Trigonometric derivatives are core senior differentiation cases.
Limit notation requires interpreting function notation and input-output language.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot parse the function expression or input variable in a limit statement.

edge.rationale: Graphical limits require understanding what input value is being approached.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the function value only rather than nearby graphical behaviour.

edge.rationale: Numerical limit estimation requires knowing the target input and nearby values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner evaluates only at the target input rather than approaching values.

edge.rationale: One-sided limits extend graphical and numerical limit interpretation from each direction.
edge.failure_signal: Learner decides a two-sided limit after checking only one side.

edge.rationale: Direct substitution requires reading the target input in limit notation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner substitutes incorrectly or applies substitution when continuity is not established.

edge.rationale: Algebraic limit simplification often uses factoring, expansion and cancellation of polynomial expressions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot simplify an expression before evaluating a limit.

edge.rationale: Continuity at a point requires determining the limiting value from both sides and comparing with the function value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner judges continuity only from whether the function is defined.

edge.rationale: Discontinuity classification requires understanding why continuity fails.
edge.failure_signal: Learner labels all discontinuities the same way without considering removable, jump or infinite behaviour.

edge.rationale: Average rate of change builds on slope as change in output over change in input.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot calculate or interpret a secant gradient over an interval.

edge.rationale: Instantaneous rate of change is approached through shrinking intervals of average rate of change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats instantaneous rate as an ordinary two-point slope over a large interval.

edge.rationale: Tangent gradient is a graphical interpretation of instantaneous rate of change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a secant line or y-value instead of tangent gradient.

edge.rationale: Derivative notation represents derivative values and derivative functions after derivative meaning is established.
edge.failure_signal: Learner manipulates symbols without knowing whether they represent a rate, tangent gradient or function.

edge.rationale: The power rule uses derivative notation to state and apply symbolic differentiation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes exponents mechanically without expressing a derivative result correctly.

edge.rationale: Termwise differentiation uses basic derivative rules such as the power rule on each term.
edge.failure_signal: Learner differentiates only one term or applies a rule across sums incorrectly.

edge.rationale: Product and quotient rules extend differentiation beyond termwise sums and differences.
edge.failure_signal: Learner distributes derivatives across products or quotients incorrectly.

edge.rationale: The chain rule requires recognising composed functions and inner/outer structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify inner and outer functions in a composite expression.

edge.rationale: Differentiating exponential and logarithmic functions requires prior knowledge of those function families.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot interpret bases, logarithms or exponential growth behaviour before differentiating.

edge.rationale: Differentiating trigonometric functions requires prior knowledge of trigonometric function behaviour.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect trig derivatives to sine, cosine and tangent graphs or units.
